notes:
Account snapshot — SlateForge builds developer platform tooling used by mid-to-large engineering teams. They want an on-prem, air-gapped code assistant integrated directly into VSCode/JetBrains (LSP-style) and CI checkers.

Key asks / constraints:
- Packaging: must support an air-gapped installer (tarball + Ansible or OVA). No outbound during install; updates via signed bundles delivered on USB or internal repo.
- Hardware sizing: target POC on 2xH100 equivalent (in their lab) but long-term expectation ~4-8x80GB GPUs for company-wide deployment; want Redwood to produce a BOM and performance estimate for 1k active devs vs 100k monthly tokens.
- Latency/streaming: interactive code completions and copilot-like streaming. SLA target: <80ms token latency p95 for single-developer sessions, batching for background linting tasks OK.
- Model/version pinning: per-repo pinning + fast rollback. Need deterministic artifact hashes and signed model bundles.
- Offline updates: quarterly security-signed bundles; must support staged rollout inside their VMs without internet.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), enterprise KMS + HSM integration for key sealing, detailed audit logs, retention controls per repo, ISO27001 + SOC2 required.
- Integration: VSCode extension + JetBrains plugin expected; prefer LSP streaming protocol. Also want gRPC/Unix-socket local agent for CLI and CI integration.

POC acceptance criteria (from CTO Aditi Rao):
- On-prem installer completes in isolated network with provided Ansible playbook.
- Streaming completion demo integrated into VSCode with p95 token latency <80ms on POC hardware.
- Model pinning and rollback operate without network access using signed bundles.
- Audit log of all inference calls visible in console and exportable.

- "We can't have the model phoning home — updates must be auditable and signed." — Aditi Rao, CTO.
- "If you can show 80ms p95 streaming in our lab we can cut a purchasing PO." — Head of SRE.
